_comment: Ported from SITTERS in Parlour v23.dc.html (line ~1440). A sitter is a job (role) crossed with a randomly-rolled sign (quirk) at encounter time — the sign is not stored here.

sitters.name: Mme Perrot
sitters.brings: The smell is not from this village. I have washed it three times and it is not from this village.
sitters.win: She washes the shirt a fourth time, then walks it to the house it came from and hands it over without a word.
sitters.fail: She stops taking laundry. The baskets stack in the yard and the yard becomes the subject.

sitters.name: Guillaume
sitters.brings: The letter was undeliverable. I did not recognise the handwriting and I did not open it.
sitters.win: He delivers it late, in person, and stays for the reading of it. Comes back the next week for nothing at all.
sitters.fail: He keeps the sack. Six months of the village goes into a cupboard and stays there.

sitters.name: Thérèse
sitters.brings: I am simply nervous, as everyone is. It is too late to say anything now anyway.
sitters.win: She says it two days before, in the kitchen, badly, and is astonished to be still standing afterwards.
sitters.fail: She marries him on the Saturday and is very composed about it for eleven years.

sitters.name: Old Marceau
sitters.brings: The plot was marked wrong on the paper. Nobody has ever asked me about it and nobody will.
sitters.win: He moves the marker himself at four in the morning and tells the family it was always where it is.
sitters.fail: He digs one more than he is asked to and will not say who for.

sitters.name: Mathis Aubert
sitters.brings: The wiring in this house is faulty. Thursdays have always been unlucky for me. I have checked everything there is to check.
sitters.win: They walk the treeline at dusk with a lamp and find the fallen cable arcing in the wet. They fix it themself, in the rain.
sitters.fail: They stop believing in Thursdays, then in wiring generally. The lamps go out one street at a time.

sitters.name: Colette Fabre
sitters.brings: There is something wrong with that child. I have never taught her anything I should not have. The mothers would never forgive it.
sitters.win: She tells the girl's mother what she did. It goes badly for an hour and well for a decade.
sitters.fail: She stops teaching. The children keep meeting anyway and invent a thirteenth sign with your face on it.

sitters.name: Ambroise Marchand
sitters.brings: It is a wolf. I have only suspected it since Tuesday. The village would never look at me the same way.
sitters.win: He does it that night, himself, and tells everyone in the morning. They respect him more, not less.
sitters.fail: Not a wolf, then. He starts butchering by intuition rather than inventory.

sitters.name: Père Renaud
sitters.brings: I do not believe in any of this. The silence was not mine to break. Eleven years of Tuesdays mean nothing.
sitters.win: He lets it go without ever telling anyone what it was, and sleeps through the night for the first time since the war.
sitters.fail: He names you from the pulpit. Not a fraud — that would be survivable — but a witch.

sitters.name: Odile Vasseur
sitters.brings: Every clock in this house runs four minutes fast. I have not touched one of them since March and nothing has come of it.
sitters.win: She sets them all right in one afternoon, starting with the one in the room she had stopped going into.
sitters.fail: She lets the whole village drift. People arrive four minutes late to everything and blame the weather.
